Recap - May 7 FS meeting - Impressions of the final meeting of the academic year were generally favorable, although there was some disappointment that not all curricular reports were approved and the JCODL legislation did not advance.
The final reports, including the Athletics presentation were informative, and the approval of the Honors legislation and UM Chapter 5 updates were important achievements.
A discussion ensued about best legislative practices, especially in terms of how floor debates proceed.
When specific concerns about or objections to legislation are known in advance, FSEC members should do their best to help resolve them before the floor is opened to discussion during a meeting.
This can include communicating with FS President and Vice President, as well as reaching out to (the) relevant committee chair(s).
Delayed decision-making about curricular reports is especially problematic at year-end, since it affects the start date for courses and programs.
Regarding the JCODL overhaul, the notice of suggested amendments was not received by all relevant parties in time to meaningfully address each point.

According to parliamentary procedure, amendments must be taken up one at a time, which is also especially unwieldy at the last meeting of the year when so much business must be attended to.
A plan for addressing the JCODL legislation in the fall was discussed and FSEC leaders will try to compile a “response to comments” document, designed to address all known objections and concerns, to be distributed with the bill in advance.
The JCODL bill will not be approved over the summer by FSEC in lieu of the full senate, because that power is reserved for emergencies.
